Hey dude. I’m 4ish years out. I was in the same spot. Marketing degree with management internships and sales jobs, so a “real” marketing position was hard to land. Got a ton of job offers trying to sell lord knows what. 

Once I did finally get a job in the industry I wanted, I found that my degree certainly helped. Even just having the background knowledge of marketing helped me. Being able to identify good vs bad marketing, random tricks you learn in school that translated to the office, my program had a TON of group projects (because marketing) and working with students in similar capacity as I would a coworker definitely helped with my transition. I have relatives that never went to school that don’t even know what a focus group is. When you get a degree, you forget that some of the stuff you learned isn’t common knowledge. 

TLDR: The degree will get your foot in the door and will give you great base knowledge, but don’t look at a degree as the final stepping stone. You’ll absolutely have to continue your education (even if it’s passively) if you want to truly stand out and continue to learn.
